name: BF-02 process fact register
source: BF-02 process fact register v1.1 (Claude Docs, 16 Oct 2026); machine copy for the Burden & Fuel Optimiser

grades.A: BF-02 trial or clean step change
grades.B: BF-02 regression or event study with a standard error

revision_log.change: OMEGA v1.1 after the out-of-sample test: GAS-14, GAS-15 replaced (per-group scales, AR(1) posterior on daily changes); GAS-17 retired (gas-capacity channel); GAS-19 (blast moisture), GAS-20 (out-of-sample test), FLOW-15, FLOW-16 (within-period resistance and stave heat load by material), DATA-11 (weather-record blast moisture) added; GAS-13, ASM-18, DATA-04, FLOW-02 notes updated.
Blend-dependent shaft efficiency (#262): GAS-13..18, ASM-18, ASM-19 added; GAS-06 and GAS-10 notes updated. No existing value changed.
Machine copy shipped with the Burden & Fuel Optimiser (#251). BAND-01: lower end implemented as a validity check, not an optimisation row (fact v1.1). No fact value changed.

Engine 2.0: RAFT from the plant workbook at the input blast moisture (DATA-03/04); BAND-01..03 enforced in code; webapp hand coefficients removed (COKE-17); COKE-14 no longer reports the ideal shaft. No fact value changed.
Register created: 17 COKE, 11 GAS, 14 FLOW, 10 DATA, 3 BAND and 13 ASM facts. Retired COKE-17 and DATA-10.

facts.statement: Shaft efficiency from the gas-flow model: ring counter-current reduction of wustite in the thermal reserve zone
facts.basis: BF-02 layered gas-flow model v0.4 (burden profile from the charging matrix, layered Ergun resistance, floating cohesive zone); six rings, eps-NTU with NTU = kappa k t_TRZ C_s / C_min; k from ISO 7215 RI and as-charged Sauter size, (11.25/d)^1.5; kappa fitted to the calibrated omega; quadratic surrogate (520-state DOE, CV omega RMSE 0.0002)
facts.literature: Rist & Meysson W-point shaft efficiency; counter-current exchanger analogy for gas-solid reduction
facts.note: Physics responses at the reference (per 10 wet pt, OMEGA v1.1 response matrix): pellet for sinter +0.0119 (kinetic +0.0081, TRZ residence +0.0037, gas/ore distribution +0.0002), pellet for Lloyds CLO +0.0213, Lloyds CLO for sinter -0.0114, NMDC ROM for sinter -0.0159, Gomti for sinter -0.0101, oversize for sinter -0.0013; fluxes and fuels move omega by less than 0.004. The blend effect is kinetic (RI and size); the blend moves the radial gas shares by less than 0.002. Pellet and lump-ore RI are literature values (no plant RI).

facts.statement: Plant-data scales on the model channels of shaft efficiency (OMEGA v1.1)
facts.basis: AR(1) Bayesian posterior of the daily change of omega against its 14-day anchor (191 days, 15 Dec 2025 - 7 Oct 2026, weather-record blast moisture): lam_pellet 1.26 +/- 0.45, lam_lump (Lloyds CLO, Geomin, NMDC ROM, Donimalai, Gomti, oversize) 0.44 +/- 0.33, operating channel 1.05 +/- 0.26; priors N(1, 0.5^2); rho 0.75. Selected out of sample (GAS-20).
facts.note: v1.0 (level regression with class corrections, lam_b 0.59 +/- 0.33) was worse than holding omega out of sample and is superseded. The lump-ore scale below 1: the data do not show the kinetic penalty of lump ore at the physics size (out-of-sample skill is highest for lump scales 0 - 0.5).

facts.statement: Pellet +10 wet pt -> shaft efficiency (OMEGA v1.1, reference operation)

The event is consistent with the model and does not narrow it.
facts.literature: Gas utilisation rises with pellet share (Indian pellets); supersedes the data-only estimate in GAS-06
facts.note: Engine (2,270 t/d, flux re-optimised): coke -4.0 kg/tHM dry from shaft efficiency for sinter (+0.3 in total with the chemistry), -5.4 for Lloyds CLO (-5.1 in total); cost +Rs 111 and +Rs 36/tHM against +Rs 241 and +Rs 210 with omega held. dK/domega -278 kg/tHM (loop-inclusive).

facts.statement: Production +1 t/h -> shaft efficiency (residence time in the thermal reserve zone)
facts.basis: Model (GAS-13): shorter TRZ residence at faster descent; data -0.0018 +/- 0.0010 (month effects), -0.0026 +/- 0.0009 (trend)
facts.literature: Shaft efficiency falls at high productivity (shorter residence)
facts.note: In blend mode the cost frontier against production is flatter: heat losses spread over more tonnes, gas utilisation falls.

facts.statement: Gas quantity -> shaft efficiency (capacity ratio R = O_max,TRZ / (Y_W n_Fe), moved by its carbon-gas part)
facts.basis: Model (GAS-13) at R 0.70, NTU about 3; solved inside the two-zone balance (rist.solve_2z omega_fn). R follows the carbon gas only: H2 reduces wustite several times faster than CO and the ring model has no gas-side rate, so H2 is not counted as extra capacity (the data show omega rising with blast moisture, +0.0035 +/- 0.0011 per g/Nm3). Amplifies coke responses by about 1.35 (dK/domega -342 against -254 kg/tHM at fixed omega): HMT +10 degC 0.94 -> 1.26, Si +0.1 % 2.0 -> 2.7 kg/tHM
facts.note: Retired 21 Oct 2026 (OMEGA v1.1): out of sample the gas-capacity channel added no skill and its data scale was negative (expanding fits -0.5 to +0.2; -2.4 +/- 0.8 against the observed change, driven by moisture and Si). R is held at the calibration (omega_model.json gas_capacity_channel false).

facts.statement: Certainty classes of a plan (blend-dependent shaft efficiency)
facts.basis: High: sigma(coke) <= 2 kg/tHM and blend classes and production inside the 1st-99th percentile of the 200 days BF-02 ran; Medium: sigma <= 5 and within 5 pt / 3 t/h of that range; Low otherwise

AR(1) posterior with GAS-14 (191 days); within months, excluding the record's monthly steps: 0.0051 +/- 0.0008. Equal to the arithmetic sensitivity of the calibrated omega to the assumed moisture (+0.0042 +/- 0.0006): the coke the balance adds for moisture (+0.8 kg/tHM per g/Nm3) is not seen in burnt coke (burnt minus model -1.2 +/- 0.2 per g/Nm3).
facts.literature: Hydrogen from blast moisture reduces wustite faster than CO; plant practice +1 g/Nm3 -> coke +0.6 to +1 kg/tHM
facts.note: Top-gas H2 shows no response to the record's day-to-day moisture (-0.001 +/- 0.005 % per g/Nm3; +0.04 - 0.05 expected). Whether the furnace's blast moisture follows the record day to day is therefore not established; the term keeps the coke prediction consistent with burnt coke either way. Net engine coke response -0.2 to -0.4 kg/tHM per g/Nm3.

facts.statement: Out-of-sample test of the shaft-efficiency model (OMEGA v1.1)
facts.basis: Day minus its 14-day anchor, 175 days 1 Jan - 7 Oct 2026; parameters from earlier days only (monthly refit). Skill = 1 - MSE/MSE(held). v1.1: omega 0.25 (day), 0.20 (7-day); burnt coke 0.175 (day, RMSE 7.4 vs 8.1 kg/tHM), 0.18 (7-day). v1.0: -0.23, -0.14, -0.29, -0.14. Time splits (train Dec-May / test Jun-Oct; reverse): v1.1 burnt coke 0.22 / 0.16 (day); v1.0 -0.22 / -0.33. Interval coverage 63 % within 1 sigma, 90 % within 1.96 sigma.
facts.note: The skill comes from the moisture term (about 0.11 in every sub-period), the operating channel and the pellet channel; without the 1 Jun, 1 Mar and 1 Oct transitions the blend channel alone has no detectable skill (within-period blend changes are 1 - 3 pt). Data-only XGBoost on the same deltas: burnt coke 0.09 (expanding), 0.34 / 0.36 (time splits); benchmark only (no mechanism for blends outside the record).
